Thanks again for the call today — useful conversation and clear success criteria. Short recap and proposed next steps below so we all stay aligned.

Call highlights:
- Goal: near real-time clinical-note summarization (inference latency target < 200ms p50, 500ms p95 for single-turn) and high fidelity for PHI-preserving extraction.
- Initial dataset: 2k anonymized notes (sample we discussed).

Recommended evaluation playbook (high level):
1) Baseline run: redwood-llm-7b-rt (FP16, uncompressed) on 1k examples — measure latency, token costs, and baseline Rouge-L.
2) Quant trade study: AWQ (8-bit asymmetric) vs GPTQ (4/8-bit mixed) vs experimental FP8 — run controlled A/B on the same samples.
3) Prompt sensitivity: run your promptset (attached catalyze_promptset_v1.json) against each model/config to observe regression patterns.
4) Canary plan: start with AWQ on a small % of traffic with a shadow evaluation and automatic rollback on quality regression > 2% absolute Rouge-L.

Attachments: call recording + promptset + short CSV template for benchmark results.

Questions for you:
- Confirm we can run evaluations on your anonymized 2k sample (share S3/GDrive link or let us stage).
- Any hard constraints on throughput vs cost (e.g., must be <= $0.02 per request)?

Next steps (proposed):

- We'll produce a short AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 trade brief and a canary rollout plan.

Subject: RE: Fwd: Recap + proposed eval plan (Catalyze) — AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 trade brief

Quick technical note & recommended plan based on similar medtech pilots we've run. Summary first, details below.

Summary (tl;dr):
- AWQ (8-bit asymmetric): best first pass for throughput gains with minimal tuning. Typical change: ~0.5–1.2% absolute F1 delta on extraction tasks vs FP16, depending on prompt sensitivity.
- GPTQ (4/8 mixed): higher compression, can give larger latency improvements but higher risk of distributional regressions; expect 1.0–2.5% F1 delta in worst-case prompts.
- FP8 (experimental): can approach FP16-like quality with optimized kernels on newer hardware (A100/NVIDIA H100); on T4-class we don't yet have mature FP8 kernel support — avoid for phase 1.

Benchmarks and expected latency (T4-class, single-turn, sequence ~120 tokens):
- redwood-llm-7b-rt (FP16 baseline): p50 ~180ms, p95 ~420ms
- redwood-llm-7b-awq (AWQ 8-bit): p50 ~120–140ms, p95 ~320–360ms
- redwood-llm-7b-gptq (mixed 4/8): p50 ~100–130ms, p95 ~300–340ms
Notes: these are ballpark numbers from prior runs; we will produce an exact CSV once we run on their sample. See preliminary benchmark: https://redwood.share/benchmarks/catalyze/2028-06-04 (attached csv).

Evaluation plan (detailed):
1) Smoke run: 200 examples across diverse note types to validate end-to-end pipeline.
2) Full push: run 1k examples through FP16 baseline, AWQ, GPTQ. Collect per-prompt metrics (F1, Rouge-L), latency percentiles, and token cost.
3) Prompt-level sensitivity: compute delta distributions and flag prompts with >2% absolute F1 drop.
4) Canary: deploy AWQ to 5% production traffic (shadow mode for GPTQ) for 72 hours; automatic rollback if rolling average F1 drop >1.5% or error rate increases >0.5%.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Prefix caching: enable short-term KV caching for repeated user contexts to reduce p95 tail.
- Per-prompt routing: for prompts flagged as sensitive, route to FP16 baseline model (automatic fallback).
- Monitoring: integrate a lightweight eval hook that samples 1% of live traffic for automated quality checks and stores traces for manual QA.

Deliverables by EOD tomorrow if dataset arrives:
- Full CSV of benchmark results (attached as benchmark-results-summary.csv).
- One-page trade brief (awq_vs_gptq-brief.pdf).
- Canary rollout runbook with rollback hooks and HubSpot playbook entry (I'll add to the deal).

Let me know if you want us to include an explicit A/B on cost per request calculation for finance/procurement.

—Karthik
